To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the coalescence plus AKK fragmentation approach correctly describes the $p_T \simeq 3 \, \rm Gev$ baryon-to-pion ratios in the range $0.5<p_T<10$ GeV.

a coalescence model, augmented with the inclusion of resonance decays, correctly describes the evolution of $p_T$ hadron spectra from RHIC energy to LHC, the baryon/meson ratios and the $p_T\phi$ ratios, and predicts a nearly $T$ independent $p_T$ spectrum for $K^0_S$ at LHC.
a coalescence model plus fragmentation functions from the literature correctly describes the $p_T \lesssim 10 \,\rm Gev$ spectra of all main hadron species in a large range of $p_T$.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the $p$ and $\Lambda$ spectra in a wide range up to $p\sim 10 \rm\,GeV$ at LHC energy and their comparison with the $\pi$ spectrum and the $p/\pi$, $\bar p/\pi$ and $p/\phi$, $\Lambda/K$ ratios.
the description of the $pT$ spectra and the baryon to meson ratios in the $p_T\sim 1-10\, GeV/c$ range.
the understanding of the $p/\phi,\bar p/\phi, \Lambda/\phi$ ratios in the $p_T> 3$ GeV region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a coalescence approach, augmented by the fragmentation of resonances and the fragmentation functions from AKK, correctly predicts the evolution from RHIC to the LHC of the main hadronic $p_T$ distributions and ratios.
coalescence plus AKK fragmentation is a successful description of hadron production from low $p_{T}$ up to $p_{T} \sim 10 \rm \,GeV$.
the coalescence plus AKK fragmentation approach is a good description of $p_T$ hadron spectra at the LHC energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the main features of hadron $p_T$ production in AA collisions can be explained in a coalesence plus fragmentation approach without the need of a new physics at RHIC and LHC energies.
coalescence plus AKK fragmentation functions can explain most of the main features observed in the $p_T-$ spectra and the baryon to meson ratios at RHIC and LHC.
a coalescence + fragmentation approach is capable to predict the evolution of $p_T$ spectrum from RHIC to the LHC energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coalescence plus hadronization model can describe the hadron production in AA collisions in a wide range in $p_T$ and energy.
coalescence is the dominant mechanism for the production of baryons in AA collisions in a wide $p_T$ region.

the coalescence plus AKK fragmentation approach correctly predicts the main features of the hadron spectra in a wide range $p_T$ and in particular the behavior of the baryon to meson ratios $p/\phi$, $p/\pi$, $p/K$ and $\Lambda/\pi$, $\Lambda/K$.
